newsitem.title: USA: Broward Cty, Fla., scraps $800 mln school bonds.
newsitem.headline: Broward Cty, Fla., scraps $800 mln school bonds.

text.p: Florida's Broward County School Board has scrapped plans for an $800 million general obligation bond referendum in November.

Instead, the board will issue $350 million of certificates of participation to make the most critical repairs and renovations this year and seek a referendum in 1998 for about $450 million of GO bonds.
The board voted late Tuesday to postpone the referendum to allow time to build credibility with voters.
A state grand jury investigation of the district's construction program is scheduled to begin Thursday, and an ongoing federal probe is also examining its construction, land and contract deals.
Additionally, a lawsuit scheduled for trial next week claims that the Broward school system built inferior schools in black neighborhoods.
School board members said the referendum was likely to fail in the current environment.
"It's very difficult to try to talk to people about the good things we are doing when every day there's a headline about the grand jury," Superintendent Frank Petruzielo said.
The $800 million bond issue would have required a property tax increase of 50 cents per $1,000 of assessed value.
